meta.note: Common surface fossils of Central Texas. Elgin sits near the boundary between Upper Cretaceous rocks (Taylor and Navarro groups) and Paleogene units (Midway and Wilcox groups); creek gravels can carry fossils from older units. Formation assignments are hypotheses unless the find came from a known outcrop. Sources: UT Bureau of Economic Geology Geologic Atlas of Texas; Finsley, A Field Guide to Fossils of Texas; Paleontological Society resources.

context: Most Central Texas fossils are marine invertebrates from Cretaceous seas (~145–66 million years ago). East of the Balcones zone, Upper Cretaceous chalks and marls (Austin Chalk, Taylor and Navarro groups) yield oysters such as Exogyra, Inoceramus clams, straight ammonites like Baculites, and shark teeth. Paleogene (Eocene/Paleocene) units hold marine shells and petrified wood.
